title: Radio, electronic switching and data processing

paras: Technology, infrastructure, network architecture, institutional ownership and business economics.
Radio transmitters, vacuum tubes, amplifiers, broadcast receivers, electromechanical switches, telex, punched cards and tabulators.

blocks.h2: Who developed, funded, owned and operated the systems?
paras: Marconi-associated companies, RCA, AT&T/Bell, IBM, broadcasters, military signals organizations, public telecom administrations. These participants had different roles: research sponsorship, equipment supply, network operation, regulation, standardization and service consumption should not be conflated.
Broadcast one-to-many transmission coexisted with switched telephone circuits and specialized point-to-point services.
Advertising-supported broadcasting, subscription telephony, equipment leasing and outsourced tabulation.
Electronic amplification expanded distance and capacity; tabulators processed coded records, but were not equivalent to stored-program computers.
Radio broadcasting sent one transmission to many receivers, unlike a telephone exchange connecting selected endpoints. Punch-card business machines encoded records for sorting and arithmetic.
Broadcast spectrum allocation, telephone concessions and wartime procurement shaped market entry, scale and standardization.
